nodes.label: to-agents-task-list Skill
nodes.rationale: A task list is a delegation contract, not a to-do list: each task is picked up by an agent with none of this conversation's context, possibly in parallel, possibly on a different model. That needs a description that stands alone, dependencies that are real, and a model sized to the task. Closes with a table, notes, and one direct ask (adjust models / adjust tasks / start the work) - a message stopping after the table leaves the contract unsigned.

nodes.label: Four-Field Task Contract
nodes.rationale: Every TaskCreate carries subject (imperative, names the outcome), description (executable by someone who never read the conversation - exact values, exact paths, the why behind arbitrary-looking constraints), blockedBy (set afterwards via TaskUpdate, real dependencies only), and metadata { complexity, model, effort, why } - the field that gets skipped, and required.

nodes.label: Size by Decisions, Not Lines
nodes.rationale: The verbs in the description you just wrote are the evidence - no separate analysis pass. Mechanical (exact outcome, typecheck proves it) gets haiku/low; standard (one layer, repo precedent to copy) gets sonnet/medium; judgment (decide/design/contract other tasks consume) gets opus/high. Escalate to xhigh/max only when judgment-level AND expensive to unwind. A 400-line mechanical port is haiku; a 12-line change to a type every module imports is opus. If you can't size it, split it.

nodes.label: Real Dependencies Only
nodes.rationale: blockedBy means cannot start, not would-rather-do-second. Real: the blocker produces a type, field, route, file or decision the blocked task reads. Verification is blocked by everything that can break it. A decision task blocks whatever the decision changes - model open questions as their own tasks. Every needless blocker is serialized time.
